runners_data.name: Halon Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Ciaran Murphy who won over this exact 7f trip on good ground last time — gets a soft lead here, though the STYLE_FIT tag notes it is technically operating slightly out of its optimal comfort zone; 40 days off but form reads fine.

runners_data.name: Dawn Romance
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who won over 6f on good ground and has placed at the trip before; headgear visor noted, six runs in similar going showing 1W3P is solid, but stepping up to 7f from 6f and needing a genuine pace to reel in from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Zenford
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Ben Coen and JP Murtagh who has posted four consecutive places over 7f including three on soft/good-to-soft — ideally suited by a tracking position behind a lone front-runner; the horse to beat if it travels sweetly.

runners_data.name: Substance
runners_data.note: Prominently ridden JP O'Brien inmate wearing a tongue-tie, returned a win over 8f on good last time and has recent experience at 7f; the high trainer strike rate (8/60 in 14 days) is a live angle and the style suits this setup well.

runners_data.name: Watch Tower
runners_data.note: George Lyons-trained prominent runner who shaped well in placed efforts over 7f at a fair track — 191 days off is a significant fitness question mark, though the yard has returned runners after breaks before; no similar-going wins to date.

runners_data.name: Chapel Lane
runners_data.note: Style unconfirmed (U), drops from 10f to 7f here for Declan McDonogh with a hood, placed twice in four runs on good ground at shorter trips — a difficult profile to map confidently, trip contraction could help or hinder.

runners_data.name: Venetian Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has placed three times at 7f and 8f on soft ground with nine runs on similar going showing 0 wins; 7 days since last run is fine, but Luke McAteer will need plenty of luck in running if the field bunches.

runners_data.name: Fortuity
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good last time for Mrs Harrington and Keithen Kennedy, and is naturally a front-runner — the field is too pace-heavy for it to secure its preferred lead, meaning it will race out of role in midfield; the STYLE_FIT discount is material here.

runners_data.name: Coincidental Glory
runners_data.note: Another natural prominent type from the Adrian McGuinness yard with a busy recent campaign (7 days since last run), but its record of 0W3P in ten runs on similar going and the redistribution to midfield against its style make it hard to strongly favour.

runners_data.name: Love Orchid
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes the mount for Noel Meade on this hold-up mare wearing a hood; no wins and 0W0P in five runs on similar going, with a step back to 7f after two 8f runs — needs things to fall right from the back.

races.paceDynamic: Halon Bay is the confirmed lone front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 7f on Good to Yielding ground at Limerick. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching — a single leader setting its own rhythm on a flat track tends to produce a strongly-run surface time but not a truly gruelling test, meaning those tracking closely will remain on the bridle deep into the race. Fortuity and Coincidental Glory are genuine prominent types who will be unable to secure their natural positions given the volume of pace-seeking runners in this field, meaning they will be shuffled wider into midfield and forced to race out of role. The race shape firmly favours horses who can sit a length or two off the lead in second or third position and kick with Halon Bay's unhurried pace in front of them — prominently ridden types who track rather than lead are the chief beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Zenford has three placed runs from three attempts on comparable going at 7f and sits in the ideal tracking position behind lone front-runner Halon Bay — if Ben Coen travels smoothly, this is the most dangerous closer.

Watch Tower is 191 days off the track and, while its prominent style suits the race shape, a fitness doubt at this level after over six months away means it may find itself under pressure sooner than expected.

Fortuity and Coincidental Glory are both natural prominent types who cannot get their preferred position in this field — monitor their post-break behaviour in the early furlongs as over-racing or interference in a bunched midfield are realistic risks.

Dawn Romance drops back from longer trips on a yielding surface that has suited her previously, but from a hold-up position needs the pace to be genuinely strong over 7f — watch how much she settles in the first two furlongs as an indicator of whether she can land the blow.

races.name: Ballyduane Stud Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Spanish Temptress
runners_data.note: Richard O'Brien's 4yo has strong similar-going form (12/15 positive) and is the race's lone pace-setter, but her OR=82 top-weight and a style tag indicating she races out of role at times should temper confidence in her sustaining it fully; 8 days fresh.|

runners_data.name: Fratas
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's 6yo returns after a huge 346-day absence (324 days since a jockey change), which is the dominant concern here; she shapes as a prominent type with solid place form at longer trips on good ground but conditioning after nearly a year off is a serious unknown.|

runners_data.name: Anvika
runners_data.note: Sheila Lavery's 5yo is a genuine hold-up type who operates at the back and depends on a truly-run race to get into it; no wins from five comparable runs but placed recently on soft, and headgear (tongue-tie) noted — trips around 8-9f on soft are her natural environment.|

runners_data.name: Gloriously Glam
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's 4yo won over 7f on good last time out wearing a hood, but her natural instinct is to come from off the pace — she has been pushed into a midfield map position because the rear is overcrowded, and her chance depends on the race developing an honest gallop.|

runners_data.name: Thru And Thru
runners_data.note: Rory Devine's 4yo carries a hold-up profile with her best recent efforts at 7f on soft; stepping to a mile on yielding is not obviously wrong, but she has never won and her six-runner sample without a win suggests she needs everything to fall right to get competitive.|

runners_data.name: Una Matata
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's 5yo has virtually no relevant form on comparable going (1/15 similar-going entries), which is a significant concern on today's Good to Yielding surface; she is a prominent type and has won over 7f on standard, but this going profile represents a real unknown.|

runners_data.name: Tofino
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's 4yo is genuinely a prominent racer but the pace map has absorbed her into midfield because there is no room at the front; she has winning form on good and is 35 days fresh, but her chance is structurally compromised if she cannot secure her natural position.|

runners_data.name: Amemri
runners_data.note: David Marnane's 6yo wears a visor and is a true hold-up type, though she finds herself mapped to midfield simply because the rear is congested; limited similar-going form (6/15) and her best efforts have come on standard surfaces — Good to Yielding may not bring out her best.|

races.paceDynamic: Spanish Temptress is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to push her from the front, she should find a comfortable, uncontested lead at a rhythm she dictates on this Good to Yielding Limerick mile. Fratas and Una Matata are the natural prominent types who will look to track her, but neither has the profile to force a contested tempo, meaning the early pace is likely to be measured rather than pressurising. The field contains a surplus of prominent and hold-up types — Tofino, Gloriously Glam, and Amemri are all redistributed on the map because there is simply insufficient room for them to fulfil their natural roles; Tofino and Gloriously Glam are most likely to secure a position close to pace, with Amemri likely to find herself further back than ideal. A sustainable gallop from Spanish Temptress sets this up as a race where a patient prominent or tracking ride that can quicken off a steady tempo has the clearest advantage — hold-up horses forced wide or back are structurally disadvantaged.

Fratas has been off the track for nearly a year and switches jockeys; watch the market move and her paddock condition closely, as a fit, well-prepared returning Fratas at OR=79 would be a serious presence.|

races.name: Greenmount Suite @ Limerick Handicap

runners_data.name: Bella Colombia
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with course form at 8f, trainer McCreery 1/18 over 14 days, went 1st on similar going in recent career which is the best evidence here, but a modest sim-going record (7/15, 0W1P) tempers expectations from the rear of the field.

runners_data.name: Crosshaven
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with a stamina concern — flagged for fading in finishes and a poor sim-going record (3/3, 0W0P), 38 days off with a short form string suggesting this trip may stretch him; trainer Murphy has had just one runner in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Green Icon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a fade-in-finish flag and a terrible recent run string of consecutive zeros; 9 days since last run for Hogan who has been active, but form figures on similar going (9/15) offer little encouragement at this trip.

runners_data.name: Limbocall
runners_data.note: Unknown style designation and 316 days off the track is the defining concern — returning from a lengthy absence for O'Callaghan, showed ability when 3rd at 8f on Good ground, but fitness and ring rustiness over a mile in a 19-runner handicap is a significant unknown.

runners_data.name: Starting Monday
runners_data.note: Prominent racer and the most natural pace partner for Racing Royalty; won over 10f on Soft for Gillian Scott and is proven on cut in the ground, though dropping back to 8f from recent miles-plus trips may sharpen him up rather than suit — watch for how quickly he asserts early.

runners_data.name: Captain Ciano
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who is dropping in trip from recent 10f outings, with a fair place record at that distance (0W1P on similar going); trainer McCourt sent him out 14 days ago and he has never really threatened in this current campaign, sitting at OR 53.

runners_data.name: Peig Sayers
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare flagged for fading in the finish, 38 days off for McLoughlin with a single runner in the same period; a dire recent sequence of 000-00 and consistent finishing positions of 10th-14th on similar ground make her hard to support.

runners_data.name: Carvalhal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a solid recent 2nd at 7f on Good ground — the most noteworthy recent piece of form in this field — trainer Burns has had no runners in 14 days, and the step back to 8f suits given her most recent placing; 5-pound claimer Nicola Burns takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Oitentinha
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer pushed into midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded — has only operated over sprint trips (5-7f) in recent history, so this step up to a mile represents an untested question over and above the style mismatch; headgear change flagged.

runners_data.name: Heart Of Darkness
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose recent form reads 200500, with his best recent effort (5th) coming at 8f on Standard; trainer McGuinness is the most active in this field (3/28 over 14 days) and the pace flag for fading is a concern, though he is racing in his best trip range — placed midfield here by necessity rather than natural positioning.

runners_data.name: Pure Valour
runners_data.note: Lightly raced hold-up type with only three runs, best effort a 6th at 10f on Good; the 45-day break and very slim form sample make assessment difficult, and being a genuine hold-up horse mapped into midfield means his natural finishing kick may not be fully utilised.

runners_data.name: Saith Seren
runners_data.note: Regular hold-up operator with a consistent pattern of mid-pack finishes (four consecutive 5ths) at trips up to 10f; the 38-day gap and jockey change to Coen are the positive angles, and she has shown she stays 8f on Soft, but the redistribution into midfield slightly compromises her ideal race shape.

runners_data.name: Liamo
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse with a win on record (1W3P from 15 runs on similar going) and a prior win at 7f on Good for Walsh; the step down in trip from recent 16f efforts is dramatic and may sharpen him — mapped midfield rather than his preferred position, which will require a clean run.

runners_data.name: Monroe Dasher
runners_data.note: 292 days off the track is the standout concern for this hold-up type, and the fade-in-finish flag compounds the worry; form shows consistent double-digit finishes on similar going and a S (slipped up) in his most recent start — hard to trust on comeback.

runners_data.name: Lady Crossing
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a 140-day layoff and all recent form on Standard/AW ground rather than turf; fade-in-finish flagged, trainer Fitzpatrick has had no runners recently, and a poor sim-going turf record (6/9, 0W0P) makes this a difficult reappearance to fancy.

runners_data.name: Bright Image
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up performer with a positive recent run (4th, 4th in last two), racing 7 days ago for Donoghue; turf form on Good is reasonable (4/10) and headgear worn — the redistribution into midfield is the main obstacle, but this is arguably the best-credentialled of the overcrowded hold-up group.

runners_data.name: Notforalongtime
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who is one of the most credible closers here, with two places from 15 runs on similar going and three recent top-5 finishes; the redistribution into midfield rather than his preferred rear position tempers the angle, though his trainer Hourigan runs him freshened up at 9 days since last run — Ben Coen is not on board here so jockey booking should be noted.

runners_data.name: Friars Gate
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer flagged for fading in the finish with four consecutive 9th-or-worse finishes; 9 days since running for Leahy, turf form on Good is poor (4/5, 0W0P at 8f), and headgear is worn — nothing in the profile suggests an imminent reversal of form.

runners_data.name: Racing Royalty
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race, setting up to dictate entirely uncontested from gate to straight; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) notes a slight positional mismatch, but as the confirmed pace-maker rather than a hold-up horse, her control of the race tempo is the defining structural factor — trainer Scott has had one winner in two runs over 14 days.

races.paceDynamic: Racing Royalty is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field on Good To Yielding ground at Limerick, and with no genuine challenger for the early lead, she is set to control the tempo from the outset without any pressure forcing her hand. The pace she sets will be measured rather than searingly quick, meaning the race is unlikely to truly develop into a genuine test for hold-up horses until well inside the final two furlongs. Starting Monday and Carvalhal are the natural prominent types who will look to sit close behind and exploit any softening in the leader, while the likes of Notforalongtime, Oitentinha, Saith Seren and several others are genuine hold-up horses who have been pushed into midfield on the map simply because the field holds more off-the-pace types than positions available at the rear — of those, Notforalongtime and Saith Seren are most likely to actually secure their favoured position given their track record of doing so. A race dominated by a lone uncontested front-runner on softening ground over a mile at this track decisively favours prominent runners who can track the pace and pounce, rather than those forced to make up ground from the back against a potentially modest tempo.

watchPoints.text: Racing Royalty sets the entire tempo unchallenged — if she is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable gallop, she could steal enough first-run advantage to hold on, and any prominent horse that fails to track her closely from the outset may run out of time to close.

With 19 runners on Good To Yielding going, there is a significant traffic risk in the final quarter-mile — hold-up horses redistributed into midfield (particularly Oitentinha, Heart Of Darkness, Pure Valour) may find their runs shut off when the field fans wide.

Carvalhal's recent 2nd at 7f on Good stands out as the form marker in this race — watch whether Nicola Burns can get the mare across to track Racing Royalty from a prominent position early, as that would put her in the ideal spot for this race shape.

Monroe Dasher and Limbocall are both returning from layoffs of over 290 days — if either shows signs of racing freshly or overreaching their fitness, they could cause interference in a compact large-field handicap on softening ground.

Starting Monday has the headgear flag (p) and ran over 10f at Southwell on his last winning start — watch whether Darragh O'Sullivan elects to use the 7lb claim aggressively to press Racing Royalty early or slots in behind, as that tactical choice will shape the race entirely.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Martin Molony Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Chally Chute
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old whose best form has come over longer trips at Cheltenham and between-the-flags, taking his natural lead role here on 229 days off — the ease of his task in front may suit, but his last notable win came over 12f on Good and the step back to a flat galloping test is not guaranteed to unlock the best of him.

runners_data.name: Cristal Clere
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan rides this eight-year-old who won over 8f at the Curragh last time and whose front-running tendencies mean he will want to race far closer than the midfield map position suggests — a trainer who has had only two runners in the last 14 days, and Good-to-Yielding form figures are blank for wins and places.

runners_data.name: Leinster
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's five-year-old has a tidy record at 14f on Good ground with three wins and four places from nine runs at the trip, and J M Sheridan's booking suggests a stalking ride — no obvious going concern and consistent in this grade.

runners_data.name: Arouet
runners_data.note: Paul Twomey's four-year-old is a natural front-runner who won over 18f on Good last summer and finished second at 12f on his return 27 days ago; James Ryan will be keen to push forward, but headgear (p) and a short prep suggests he may not get the prominent pitch his form demands.

runners_data.name: Happy Pharoah
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's four-year-old has a fine prominent-racing record at 14f on Good (3W 5P from 10 runs), wears a tongue-tie, and Paddy Harnett keeps it simple — the two-year-old win over 13f on Good and the course of recent form suggest he is well-placed for this trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Layfayette
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's nine-year-old is a genuine hold-up type whose last two runs showed a wide spread (6th then 2nd over 16f and 14f), and Adam Caffrey will be patiently ridden from off the pace — no wins on Good to Yielding specifically across the past 15 runs in similar conditions is a flag.

runners_data.name: Sunchart
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery, this nine-year-old comes here on 55 days off with a mixed recent profile (7-3-8-17 in last four) but has two wins in similar-going conditions across 13 similar runs — a genuine hold-up runner who needs a genuine gallop to set up his late challenge from the back.

runners_data.name: Uxmal
runners_data.note: Another O'Brien-trained prominent racer returning after 229 days off, whose three wins include a 22f Chester win on Good and 14f wins on Soft — stamina is not in question, but the long absence and the fact he was pulled up on his last start are concerns that Nathan Crosse will need to manage from a prominent berth.

runners_data.name: Goodie Two Shoes
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh partners this seven-year-old for Joseph Patrick O'Brien, and the form record is outstanding — five wins from 15 runs in similar going conditions, a 2/3/1/1/1 last-five with three of those on Good at 14-16f, and a tongue-tie adds the finishing touch; the distance, going and race shape all align neatly.

runners_data.name: Bubble Gum
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners J P Murtagh's five-year-old who won over 12f at the Curragh on his most recent winning run, but the last four runs have been disappointing — his natural push-forward tendency places him in a crowded prominent group where he is unlikely to secure his preferred berth, and OR 97 is the lowest rated in this company.

runners_data.name: That's Amore
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old won on the all-weather at Southwell and over 8f at Haydock, and Luke McAteer takes the ride — limited form on turf going similar to today's (0W 0P from 2 runs) and stepping up sharply in class to Listed level; front-running by nature but squeezed out of that role by the depth of pace in this field.

runners_data.name: New Zealand
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old receives a weight concession of 11lb from the top weights and won over 7f on Good last year, but has not won since and the step up to 1m4½f is unexplored — Jack Cleary gets the ride and the youth and light weight could factor in a muddling finish, though he is another prominent type who cannot get his natural position.

races.paceDynamic: Chally Chute is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival willing to take him on — he should be able to slide into a comfortable, rhythm-dictating lead at whatever tempo suits Ross O'Sullivan's plan. With Good To Yielding ground confirmed across the card at Limerick, a moderate-to-honest gallop is the most likely outcome, which keeps the race together until the home straight and places a premium on those who can race prominently behind the leader before quickening. Prominent types — Goodie Two Shoes, Leinster, Happy Pharoah and Uxmal — are therefore ideally placed to exploit a sustainable gallop, sitting just off Chally Chute and having first use of any acceleration. This race shape unambiguously favours the close-tracking prominent racer with class and stamina: true hold-up horses Layfayette and Sunchart will be fighting traffic from deep, and the redistributed prominent types who have been mapped further back than their nature demands face an additional tactical headwind in a field that is far more pace-laden than the single on-paper front-runner suggests. The field contains far more genuinely prominent types than can all secure a forward pitch — Cristal Clere, New Zealand, Arouet, Bubble Gum and That's Amore are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who are mapped to midfield by necessity, and of those Cristal Clere (Seamie Heffernan) and Arouet (Paul Twomey yard) are most likely to actually push forward and secure a position close to the pace.

watchPoints.text: Goodie Two Shoes arrives with the most complete profile in the race — five wins on comparable going, Declan McDonogh in the saddle, and O'Brien's stable in form (8 winners from 62 runners in 14 days) — watch whether he gets a clean, uncrowded run from a prominent position.

The sheer number of displaced prominent types (Cristal Clere, Arouet, New Zealand, Bubble Gum, That's Amore) means the early stages could be more contentious than the single front-runner profile implies — watch the first two furlongs for unexpected pace injection that could scramble the pace map entirely.

Uxmal and Chally Chute both return after 229-day absences — watch the market moves for both in the final hour, as fitness questions over horses returning from that length of layoff could dramatically affect the unfolding of the pace.

Layfayette and Sunchart are the only true hold-up horses in the race and both lack recent wins on Good to Yielding — if the pace is merely fair rather than truly searching, watch whether they are able to close at all from off the pace at Limerick's flat, right-handed track.

Happy Pharoah wears a tongue-tie and has been placed in four of five 14f Good-ground starts — watch whether Paddy Harnett opts to push him forward early given the crowded prominent group, as a battle for position between him, Leinster and the redistributed types could compromise more than one chance.

races.name: McMahons Builders Providers Maiden

runners_data.name: Faithful Follower
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old handicapper running off OR 120 with Seamie Heffernan booked, showing a win and three places over similar going (12/14 sim-going runs); genuine hold-up horse by nature whose best chance depends on the pace being strong enough to close into — 45 days off and a drop to maiden company is an interesting yard angle from Paul Hennessy.

runners_data.name: It's Good To Talk
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type for Emmet Mullins who has run twice at 10f on Good ground recently without threatening; the fade flag is a real concern over a longer 1m4½f trip, and a trainer strike rate of 0/6 over 14 days adds little confidence.

runners_data.name: Wrob And Wryan
runners_data.note: A 7-day turnaround for Andrew Lee's five-year-old, whose recent form over shorter trips on Good and Soft reads poorly (5005-0); held-up by nature but with limited scope to land in a genuine rear position given the field's composition, and the form figures offer nothing to recommend him.

runners_data.name: An Cailleach
runners_data.note: John C McConnell's four-year-old has run only twice, both on Soft ground over 10f, finishing 12th and 17th — raw and unproven at 1m4½f; wears a hood, which may help concentration, but the form is too thin to trust and the hold-up style leaves her reliant on a pace that may not materialise.

runners_data.name: Taj Crown
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner for K J Condon and Ben Coen, wearing a visor and carrying OR 68; a placed effort over 12f on Good is the standout piece of relevant form in the race, and a solo lead at a controlled pace over this trip is his clearest route to a big run.

runners_data.name: Cascade Canyon
runners_data.note: Kevin Thomas Coleman's three-year-old drops to a 1m4½f maiden after four runs over 10-12f without threatening; hold-up in style but, given the density of closers, getting into a truly rear position is unlikely — the form (6040) gives limited grounds for optimism.

runners_data.name: Ravens Can Fly
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery three-year-old with only two runs (both on Good, both unplaced) carrying a fade flag; the 7-day turnaround and trainer's recent 3/30 strike rate are modest, and there is nothing in the profile to suggest a step forward at this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Royal Sapphire
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's three-year-old drops in distance relative to some runs but steps up to 1m4½f for the first time; wears blinkers, has run seven times without troubling the judge and carries a finish-fade flag — the redistribution from true hold-up to midfield further limits the chance.

runners_data.name: Second Line
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's three-year-old returns after 38 days off with Nathan Crosse aboard; the form figures of 8-8-10 are modest and the fade flag is noted, though the yard's 6/34 recent strike rate and the extra distance could unlock something in an unexposed maiden if stamina proves the key.

runners_data.name: Blissful Bonita
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's three-year-old has the most consistent recent form in the field (568-75 including a 5th over 12f on Good) and wears a hood; an unknown running style (U) makes her tactically flexible, and a 9-day turnaround with a 2/34 yard strike rate represents a live outside chance.

runners_data.name: Mare Crisium
runners_data.note: Lightly raced K J Condon filly with only two runs (8th on Heav, 6th on Soft over shorter trips); the unknown style makes her difficult to place in the pace map, but the lightly-raced flag and stable connection with Taj Crown merit watching — untapped stamina over 1m4½f is a possibility.

runners_data.name: Themis
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's three-year-old has form figures of 0-709 with a fade flag; the best visible figure is a 7th over 8f on Heavy, and stepping up to 1m4½f on Good To Yielding is a significant ask — the sheer number of hold-up types ahead of her on the map limits her scope to operate from her natural position.

runners_data.name: Tintinabulla
runners_data.note: Ms Sheila Lavery's three-year-old has run only twice (8th on Soft, 14th on Good) and carries a fade flag; the 15-day gap and a trainer strike rate of 0/7 over 14 days offers little encouragement, and the step up in trip looks optimistic given the current level of form.

races.paceDynamic: Taj Crown is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner maiden over 1m4½f on Good To Yielding ground at Limerick, and with no credible challenger likely to press for the lead, Ben Coen can dictate an uncontested, fully-controlled tempo. At a distance where Taj Crown has already shown a placed effort (2nd over 12f on Good), a sustainable gallop is the most likely race shape — one that rewards horses who can travel prominently and have the stamina to quicken from a handy position in the straight rather than those making up ground late. The field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types, yet Faithful Follower, An Cailleach, Cascade Canyon, Wrob And Wryan, Royal Sapphire and Themis are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers for the race shape to accommodate them all at the rear. This race shape most directly favours Taj Crown and any runner willing to press into second or third on the first circuit, as the lone-leader scenario creates a pace vacuum that late closers — most of whom are not genuinely hold-up types anyway — will struggle to bridge on this ground.

watchPoints.text: Taj Crown is the lone front-runner — watch whether Ben Coen elects to dictate from the front or allows another runner to push forward, as the entire pace shape of this race pivots on that decision at the break.

Faithful Follower (Seamie Heffernan, OR 120, 45 days off) is a legitimate class runner dropping into a maiden, but is a true hold-up horse who needs genuine pace to close into — if Taj Crown crawls, his chance evaporates regardless of ability.

An Cailleach, Cascade Canyon and Themis are all true closers who are unlikely to secure their natural rear position given the concentration of hold-up horses in this field — watch for them to race closer than usual, which could compromise their finishing effort.

The going is officially Good To Yielding throughout the card at Limerick — notably softer than the race card's Good To Soft descriptor — which could meaningfully affect stamina requirements over 1m4½f and favour horses with proven soft-ground form over those exposed only on quick ground.

Blissful Bonita (hood, unknown style, Gavin Cromwell) is the one runner whose tactical flexibility could allow her to slot into whatever gap the pace map creates — watch her position in the first furlong as a guide to how the midfield order settles.

races.name: Racing Again On 2nd July Handicap

runners_data.name: Quatre Bras
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Richard O'Brien, 47 days off and limited recent form (just one placing from five recent runs in similar going), making this a watch-and-see reappearance more than a banker; trip looks fine but the soft form record is patchy.

runners_data.name: Satono Chevalier
runners_data.note: Back in just 18 days off consecutive wins at 13f and 10f, Paddy Harnett (5lb claim) is a useful booking, and the step back up in trip to 1m4½f brings it back to a distance it has handled; a horse to take seriously in any scenario where the pace is fair and the field runs straight.

runners_data.name: Slurricane
runners_data.note: Won over this trip only 7 days ago and returns with fitness on its side under Nathan Crosse; the soft-going record is extensive but victory remains elusive in similar conditions, and the very quick turnaround on yielding ground over this trip is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Dark Summit
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Denis Hogan flagged with a tendency to fade in the finish, which is a structural concern in any scenario here; the form figures on good and good-to-soft are poor, and 40 days off without a placing does little to inspire confidence at this trip.

runners_data.name: Genoah
runners_data.note: Placed in a 12f and 10f on standard going for M D O'Callaghan, Jamie Powell takes the ride; this is naturally a prominent-racing horse that will be squeezed toward midfield by the congestion at the front — its chance is most meaningful only if it can recover its natural position, which its STYLE_FIT tag suggests is unlikely in this shape.

runners_data.name: Dawn Coming
runners_data.note: Adam Caffrey comes in for a horse returning from 243 days off (92 days since jockey's last ride on it), and while Dawn Coming is a thorough stayer with a fine record in soft/yielding conditions at long distances, it is a true prominent type that will struggle to secure that position with so many rivals wanting the same ground.

runners_data.name: Palace Rock
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old back from 819 days absent (509 since jockey last rode it) for Francis Casey, and while it boasts soft-ground form and stays well, the layoff is extreme and this is a horse naturally suited to taking an early position — one it will find difficult to claim here given the competition for prominent slots.

runners_data.name: Chemdawg
runners_data.note: Brings soft-ground and staying experience from Oliver McKiernan's yard, returning after 235 days off; it is inherently a horse that wants to race up with the pace, but with several rivals ahead of it in the queue for prominent positions, it is likely to find itself racing further back than ideal — a genuine out-of-role risk.

runners_data.name: Eben Zaabeel
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes the ride for A J Martin, and while Eben Zaabeel is a hold-up type on a six-run losing streak, the 19-day turnaround is positive and the yielding ground should suit the 5yo better than the good ground it has faced recently; one whose profile at least matches a pace scenario where the front end tires.

runners_data.name: Battle Of Maldon
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's three-year-old won over 10f on soft last time and holds a prominent racing style; Declan McDonogh is a strong booking and this horse's youth and rating (OR 82, top of the weights) makes it the most interesting profile in the field if it can settle just off the pace in second or third — the trip is longer than its winning form but the soft ground and trainer form (T14: 8/48) give context.

runners_data.name: Mighty Wave
runners_data.note: J S Bolger's three-year-old is lightly raced, hold-up in style, and Andrew Slattery rides; form is limited to three starts and the long 1m4½f trip is unexplored territory, making this a speculative entry whose profile best suits a late-run scenario — upside limited by inexperience, downside by the trip.

runners_data.name: Omniscient
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner here despite being the confirmed front-runner; if Omniscient does not line up, the race loses its sole pace-maker and the entire dynamic shifts dramatically toward a contest with no natural leader — a significant caveat over the whole pace map.

races.paceDynamic: Omniscient is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with a clear lead from the off over 1m4½f on Good To Yielding ground at Limerick, is set to dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop that suits a horse who can settle and finish. Quatre Bras, Satono Chevalier, Slurricane, and Battle Of Maldon are all natural prominent racers, but the field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Genoah, Dawn Coming, Palace Rock, and Chemdawg are genuine prominent horses redistributed to midfield, and of those Genoah and Battle Of Maldon are most likely to actually press forward and secure a position close to the pace. With Omniscient unlikely to be strongly pressured early, the race is likely to be run at a steady-to-fair clip, with a single controlled surge in the home straight rather than a war of attrition from the front. This shape strongly favours horses with a prominent-to-midfield profile that can sit within striking range on a conservative pace and produce a sustained finish — pure hold-up horses launching from the rear are at a structural disadvantage here.

watchPoints.text: Omniscient is listed as a non-runner — if confirmed absent, the race has no genuine front-runner and the entire pace shape collapses, with no horse naturally suited to lead and the contest becoming a slow-run scramble that punishes the whole analysis.

Battle Of Maldon is the highest-rated horse in the field (OR 82) with a sharp jockey booking in Declan McDonogh, and its natural prominent style means it could easily press to the front if Omniscient is absent — monitor market support as a strong indicator of race leadership.

Genoah, Dawn Coming, Palace Rock, and Chemdawg are all genuine prominent horses who cannot all get their preferred position; watch the early exchanges for jostling and any unexpected surge in pace as these four compete for slots behind the leader.

Satono Chevalier returns just 18 days after back-to-back wins and the form at this distance is workable — if Paddy Harnett settles it smoothly in third or fourth on the fence, it is a live danger in any scenario where the pace is fair and the straight is run on stamina.

The going is officially Good To Yielding at Limerick for the 8:10, consistent with every race on the card — conditions are predictable and no horse faces a surprise surface, but those with a proven record in this range (Dawn Coming's yielding form figures stand out) have a genuine advantage over horses running on it for the first time.
